::: {.custom-box}
To study convergence in $m$, we keep the spatial mesh size $h$ and time step $\tau$ fixed. Theorem `lastlasttheorem` in `paper/main.tex` gives
$$
E\lesssim\tau+h^{\alpha-\epsilon}
+h^{\alpha-2}\exp\!\left(-2\pi\sqrt{(1-\alpha/2)m}\right),
\qquad 0<\alpha<2.
$$
The rational contribution therefore has reference slope $S_m=-2\pi\sqrt{1-\alpha/2}$ in a regression of $\ln E$ against $\sqrt{m}$. This is an upper-bound prediction for that contribution, rather than a guaranteed slope of the total error. Temporal, spatial, and reference-quadrature errors can produce a plateau as $m$ increases; their sizes should be checked independently.
For the experimental equation $u_t+\nu L^{\alpha/2}u=f$, keep $\nu>0$ fixed along each curve; constants can depend on it. This implementation is being tested before updating the paper.
:::


```{r, eval = TRUE}

```{r}
# Parameters: shared scientific and numerical settings live in fun/convergence_settings.Rmd.
run_id <- NULL # Set an existing ID to load that run with matching settings.
settings <- convergence_settings("m")
invisible(list2env(settings, envir = environment()))

run_dir <- experiment_run("m", experiment_parameters, run_id = run_id,
                          execution = execution_settings)
cat("Shared suite:", experiment_parameters$suite_id, "\nRun ID:", basename(run_dir), "\nResults:", run_dir, "\n")
```

All three studies read `fun/convergence_settings.Rmd`. Match the profile and
shared-suite fingerprint when comparing results. The analytic reference and
space-time error norm are common; no fine reference space-time mesh is needed.
The shared coefficient source chooses fixed m=4 for `"package"` or m=8 for
`"computed"`, and automatically selects the m study's auxiliary grids.
The default computed pilot uses T=1 and diffusion=1 in all three studies.
Runs are saved outside this code repository under
`~/Desktop/DOCS/NAFDEMG/diffusion_experiments/`.
The independent shared `m_max` setting defaults to 4 for the m study;
raising it to 5--8 leaves the h/tau fixed order at 8 for computed coefficients.
The default uniform-modal backend evaluates the same FEM/backward Euler
recurrence on uniform tadpole meshes without enumerating every time step.
Actual mesh sizes and time steps are saved and plotted. Refinement checks
separate accuracy checks from intentional refinement of the study variable.
The m study also reports its spatial-temporal floor relative to the total error.
A failed accuracy check means the fitted rate needs further calibration.
Independent cases use persistent workers. The direct backend advances through
time and reuses bounded spatial and temporal caches. The uniform-modal backend
uses scalar recurrences and quadrature, without a large temporal cache. The
coordinator alone saves results. Read `resources.csv` for per-job timings and
observed worker memory; `worker_log.txt` records worker startup and direct-solver
progress. Execution settings do not change the numerical parameters used to
validate a saved run.

```{r, eval = FALSE, class.source = "fold-show"}
# Refuse to overwrite an existing run before starting any expensive work.
stopifnot(!file.exists(file.path(run_dir, "results.rds")))
results <- run_tadpole_study(
  study = "m", axis_values = axis_values, alpha_vector = alpha_vector,
  time_grids = list(time_grid), fixed_h = h_fixed,
  anchor_h = anchor_h, anchor_grid = anchor_grid, anchor_m = anchor_m,
  diffusion = diffusion, kappa = kappa, modes = active_modes, N_finite = N_finite,
  initial = exact_initial, forcing = exact_forcing, A = AAA, omega = OMEGA,
  quadrature_order = quadrature_order, run_refinement_checks = run_refinement_checks,
  refinement_tolerance = refinement_tolerance, workers = workers,
  temporal_cache_mib = temporal_cache_mib, memory_budget_gib = memory_budget_gib,
  worker_log = file.path(run_dir, "worker_log.txt"),
  solver_backend = solver_backend, step_sum_order = step_sum_order,
  root_interpolation = root_interpolation, coefficient_source = coefficient_source)
results$parameters <- experiment_parameters
errors_projected <- results$errors_projected
checks <- results$refinement_checks
save_experiment_results(results, run_dir)
write.csv(results$diagnostics, file.path(run_dir, "rational_diagnostics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(checks, file.path(run_dir, "refinement_checks.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(results$resources, file.path(run_dir, "resources.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(results$execution, file.path(run_dir, "execution.rds"))
print(results$execution)
print(results$diagnostics)
print(checks)
if (nrow(checks) && any(checks$required & !checks$passed))
  message("Accuracy checks failed: inspect refinement_checks.csv before using these rates.")
```

```{r}
# Load only this run; metadata must match the parameters above.
results <- load_experiment_results(run_dir)
errors_projected <- results$errors_projected
```

```{r}
observed_rates <- numeric(length(alpha_vector))
for (u in 1:length(alpha_vector)) {
  observed_rates[u] <- coef(lm(log(errors_projected[, u]) ~ sqrt(m_vector)))[2]
}

theoretical_rates <- -2 * pi * sqrt(1 - alpha_vector / 2)

p_m_tadpole <- error.convergence.plotter(x_axis_vector = m_vector, 
                                 alpha_vector, 
                                 errors_projected, 
                                 theoretical_rates, 
                                 observed_rates,
                                 line_equation_fun = exp_line_equation,
                                 fig_title = expression("Convergence in " * italic(m)),
                                 x_axis_label = expression(italic(m)),
                                 apply_sqrt = TRUE)

p_m_nicer_tadpole <- errorConvergencePlotterLatex(x_axis_vector = m_vector, 
                                 alpha_vector, 
                                 errors_projected, 
                                 theoretical_rates, 
                                 observed_rates,
                                 line_equation_fun = exp_line_equation,
                                 fig_title = "$\\mbox{Convergence in }m$",
                                 x_axis_label = "$m\\quad(\\sqrt{\\phantom{x}}\\mbox{ scale})$",
                                 y_axis_label = "$\\|u-U_{h,m}^{\\tau}\\|_{L_2(\\Gamma\\times[0,T])}\\quad(\\log_{\\mathrm{e}}\\mbox{ scale})$",
                                 color_label = "$\\quad\\quad\\;\\;\\alpha\\;|\\;\\phantom{-}\\mathtt{theo}\\;|\\;\\;\\phantom{-}\\mathtt{obs}\\;\\;|\\%\\mathtt{re}$",
                                 apply_sqrt = TRUE)

ggsave(file.path(run_dir, "conv_rates_m_tadpole.png"), width = 4, height = 5, plot = p_m_tadpole, dpi = 300)
myggsave(p_m_nicer_tadpole, width = 4, height = 5, use_mathpazo = TRUE,
         output_dir = file.path(run_dir, "tikzpic"), copy_to_presentation = FALSE)
save(p_m_tadpole, file = file.path(run_dir, "p_m_tadpole.RData"))
save(p_m_nicer_tadpole, file = file.path(run_dir, "p_m_nicer_tadpole.RData"))
```


```{r, eval = FALSE, fig.align='center', out.width="400px", out.height="500px", fig.cap = captioner("Comparison between theoretical and observed convergence behavior for the $L_2(\\Gamma\\times(0,T))$-error with respect to $m$ on a semi-$\\text{log}_{e}$ scale, with $m$ plotted on a square-root scale. Dashed lines indicate the theoretical rates, and solid lines represent the observed error curves. The legend below each plot shows the value of $\\alpha$ along with the corresponding theoretical ('theo'), and observed ('obs') rates for each case.")}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(run_dir, "tikzpic", "p_m_nicer_tadpole_with_mathpazo.pdf"))
```
